correctness.rationale: The projected endpoint column has exact reproduced moments (mass one, first and second moments zero). Its Gini variation equals n-1 plus twice the sum of upward pairwise inversions. Zero inversions imply monotonicity, whose first and second weighted moment constraints force the column to equal the impulse, contradicting impulse nonmembership in the fitted subspace. Constant, affine, and interpolation cases are computed separately. Degree-two row identity and integral asymptotic 189/125 follow from an explicit orthogonal basis and an exact integral; an independent rational Gram inversion and exhaustive finite binary-cut test corroborate the four-node sharp coefficient and boundary cases. The fixed-impulse asymptotic is not claimed sharp.

value.rationale: The all-degree boundary answers a natural question about whether global polynomial least-squares fitting reduces unweighted pairwise signal dispersion. The basis-free moment obstruction applies to every quadratic-reproducing orthogonal subspace excluding an endpoint atom, and the exact asymptotic impulse ratio 189/125 proves a persistent large-sample effect. These structural statements are not a cosmetic restatement of Euclidean projection contractivity or an arbitrary finite-data computation.
